source.title: Communication-Efficient Adaptive Batch Size Strategies for Distributed Local Gradient Methods
source.authors: Tim Tsz-Kit Lau; Weijian Li; Chen-Wei Xu; Han Liu; Mladen Kolar

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares adaptive local batch sizing with constant batch sizes and reports validation performance under fixed training budgets, a different strategy aimed at the large-batch generalization gap.
record.gate_note: Rows capture reported validation outcomes for adaptive and constant batch schedules. The paper also cites prior work on large-batch training; those cited results are not rows. The CIFAR-10 and ImageNet tables provide sufficient comparisons; C4 results and other CIFAR-10 settings are left out due to the 60-row limit.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance across constant and adaptive batch sizes under fixed sample budgets: 600 epochs on CIFAR-10, 200 epochs on ImageNet, and approximately four billion tokens on C4. These results test V5 in distributed local training.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: adaptive local batch sizing reduces the large-batch held-out performance penalty with modest additional training time. It does not consistently recover smaller-batch performance; ImageNet results explicitly retain a gap.
record.recipe_differences: Uses adaptive local batch sizes with Local SGD or AdamW and compares them with constant batch schedules; it does not reproduce the cited large-batch methods. Experiments vary local steps and adaptive threshold η.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on the number of local steps H and adaptive threshold η. ImageNet reports the gap growing with H. CIFAR-10 appendix reports three-seed variability for validation accuracy.
record.problems: The ImageNet table reports no uncertainty estimates. The paper uses validation accuracy/loss as its generalization measure; it does not report train-test error gaps directly. CIFAR-10 reports three-seed standard deviations, and the authors note that adaptive schedules vary across seeds.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted C4 validation-loss comparisons from Section 6.2 and Appendix C.2, and the remaining ResNet-50 CIFAR-10 schedule settings from Table 1 and Appendix Table 4, to remain within 60 rows. These results compare adaptive and constant batch schedules under fixed training budgets.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons and tuning regimes.

Longer-training remedies, isolated effects of learning-rate scaling or warmup, normalization or regularization changes, and precise workload-dependent thresholds. Scaling and warmup are used, but their effects are not separately tested.
Controlled dropout and weight-decay removal comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with other measures.
Removal of memorized versus randomly selected examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: CIFAR-10 extraction mixes Table 4 blocks: R1–R3 are H=4, R4–R6 are H=1, and R7–R12 are H=16. All reported numeric values are present, but these condition and baseline errors change their interpretation. C4 and remaining CIFAR-10 results are tested, explicitly declared omissions, so they are neither untested nor undeclared missing results. C4 Table 6 also contains apparent inconsistencies with Table 2 and within its reported steps, warranting source review before extraction. Residual penalties after adaptation do not limit V5, which already allows partial mitigation. Held-out performance comparisons do not isolate optimization error from train–test generalization gaps.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Language-model fixed-budget results on C4; exact workload-dependent batch threshold; recipe adjustments involving learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization or regularization.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
